question: May failed native Codex rollout stderr/stdout be copied into persisted trajectory and agent-event diagnostics after bounded sanitization, or must emission be limited to structured status and correlation fields?
rationale: The patch crosses a sensitive boundary from Codex-owned rollout records into OpenClaw-visible persisted and emitted diagnostics; tests can validate a chosen policy but cannot choose how much free-form native text is acceptable.

options.title: Structured fields only
options.body: Emit correlation IDs, status, success, change kinds, and scan metadata while omitting free-form stderr/stdout previews from persisted or agent-visible diagnostics.

options.title: Allow hardened previews
options.body: Permit bounded previews only after cross-platform default-deny redaction, adversarial tests, exact Codex contract confirmation, and a redacted live canary.

options.title: Pause rollout scanning
options.body: Keep current projection diagnostics and close or redesign this PR if reading private rollout files is not an accepted runtime boundary.

recommendation.title: Structured fields only
recommendation.body: Emit correlation IDs, status, success, change kinds, and scan metadata while omitting free-form stderr/stdout previews from persisted or agent-visible diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex integration history makes this the best available owner for deciding the rollout-to-trajectory security boundary.
